- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., sentiment > 0.6) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., sentiment < 0.4) — model fails to capture downward pressure or mean reversion.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment drops, forecast remains elevated.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and underweights lows — correct by smoothing out extreme deviations in 30-day forecast.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is rising — adjust downward by 1–2% for early horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.3–0.7), model overfits short-term momentum — dampen forecast volatility by reducing standard deviation of 30d forecast.
